answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, the agent network filters admittance at an ingress wharf using graph-theoretic trust routing. Entrants must route verifiable trust paths to basalt anchor nodes via an opal credential ledger, forcing an attacker to secure scarce, non-forgeable trust endorsements from honest peers. This bounds Sybil propagation by the topological cut capacity. However, it disenfranchises honest peripheral agents with sparse connections and remains vulnerable to collusive infiltration.
